accessibility: Painting stages carry an sr-only heading or ordered list with the words their captions show one at a time; visual captions are aria-hidden.
Every painting stage is marked data-guide-cover so the guide card stays off it.
The viewer is a native modal dialog; html:has(dialog[open]) stops page scroll.
Skip link is a solid button revealed on focus; focus ring 2px tone accent, offset 3px.
Without JS, [data-reveal] content is forced visible; without WebGL, SMK photographs stand in for the figures and the plain painting image stays.
conventions.provenance: Every shipping raster carries provenance written by `impeccable embed-prompt` (origin, licence, processing, use): a <file>.json sidecar beside each WebP in public/paintings (including depth maps, SAM cut-out layers and LaMa-filled plates), public/statues and public/projects/plates; an impeccable:prompt metadata entry embedded in PNG and JPEG files (project screenshots, og-image.jpg).
conventions.roomSigns: One capitalised Ancient Greek noun per room with transliteration and gloss in both languages: ΛΟΓΟΣ, ΟΔΥΣΣΕΙΑ, ΜΕΘΟΔΟΣ, ΤΕΧΝΗ, ΜΑΝΤΕΙΟΝ, ΕΡΓΑ, ΓΙΓΑΝΤΟΜΑΧΙΑ, ΧΑΙΡΕ; lang="el", above the local title in one heading; size capped by letter count (--glyphs) to fit phones.
conventions.roomOrder: Hero (Cole) -> ΛΟΓΟΣ (Plato) -> ΟΔΥΣΣΕΙΑ (Rubens, Homer) -> ΜΕΘΟΔΟΣ (Bayeu) -> ΤΕΧΝΗ (discus thrower) -> ΜΑΝΤΕΙΟΝ (Miola) -> ΕΡΓΑ (Church's Parthenon, colonnade) -> ΓΙΓΑΝΤΟΜΑΧΙΑ (Jordaens, animated) -> ΧΑΙΡΕ (Apollo); paintings and figures alternate.

narrative.overview:
The site is a walk through the city of Thomas Cole's *The Consummation of Empire* (1836) late in the day. Every colour is taken from that painting: the hazy sky is the page's ground, sunlit marble carries labels, gilding marks what matters, and the umber of its deepest shade becomes the portico where the works stand, open onto Frederic Church's Parthenon. Rooms follow one another down a single scroll; each holds a marble cast from SMK's Royal Cast Collection, or a full-screen painting, standing in haze until the visitor's arrival lets the sun find it.

Depth is light, not chrome. Figures are lit in WebGL by a moving sun, a sky fill and a warm bounce; paintings are drawn from a depth map so near things move against far ones, the light relights their relief and the distance dissolves into the ground first. Text obeys the same law: it comes out of the haze as the room's light rises. Surfaces are square, flat slips of marble and hairlines of stone; there are no cards, no glass, no accent neon.

Density is low and the pacing is architectural: a room is a viewport or more, with the sign set large and the reading column narrow. Everything still reads with JavaScript, WebGL or motion off.
keyCharacteristics: One palette, from one painting: sky ground, umber ink, gilding, sunlit marble, portico shade.
Two tone contexts: umber on the sky, marble in the shade; components read tones, never fixed colours.
Light and haze are the only gradients and the only motion grammar.
Museum cartelas with real collection data are the component language.
Bilingual room signage: the Greek name in flared Commissioner, the visitor's language beneath.
Square corners everywhere; hairlines instead of boxes.

rules.name: The One Painting Rule
rules.body: Every colour on the page exists in Cole's painting. A new colour needs a source in one of the site's paintings, not in a UI kit.

rules.name: The Tone Context Rule
rules.body: Components read `tone`, `tone-soft`, `tone-mute`, `tone-line`, `tone-accent` and `tone-ground`, never ink or marble directly. On the sky (`:root`) the tones resolve to umber, stone and deep gold over the sky; inside `.on-shade` they resolve to marble, shade line and light gold over the portico shade. The only fixed-colour components are the cartela family (always marble and ink) and the ink button (always umber with marble).

rules.name: The Gold Ladder Rule
rules.body: Gold is chosen by what it sits on: gilding for fills and lines, deep gold for type on the sky, gilding-for-ink for small type over a painting's sky, light gold for type in shade.

rules.name: The Flare Axis Rule
rules.body: Signage flares, reading never does. Body sets FLAR 0; narration over a painting takes a little flare (FLAR 50 for the giants' lines, 60 for the oracle's step titles), the hero tagline FLAR 70, the about statement FLAR 80, Greek signs and the method's step numerals FLAR 100.

rules.name: The Own Slant Rule
rules.body: Transliterations lean on Commissioner's slant axis (slnt -10), never a synthesized italic.

rules.name: The One Name Rule
rules.body: Cormorant SC is the name's face and nothing else's.

rules.name: The Room Sign Naming Rule
rules.body: Each room carries one capitalised Ancient Greek noun with its transliteration and gloss: ΛΟΓΟΣ (about), ΟΔΥΣΣΕΙΑ (experience), ΜΕΘΟΔΟΣ (method), ΤΕΧΝΗ (skills), ΜΑΝΤΕΙΟΝ (the oracle), ΕΡΓΑ (projects), ΓΙΓΑΝΤΟΜΑΧΙΑ (the battle of the giants), ΧΑΙΡΕ (contact). The Greek is marked `lang="el"`, sits above the existing local-language title as part of the same heading, and never replaces it.

rules.name: The Light and Haze Rule
rules.body: Light and haze are the only gradients. Anything the sun has not reached dissolves into its room's ground: figures through the haze uniform, paintings distance-first through their depth map, text through `--room-light` mixing its colour toward the ground. Vapour, storm cloud and lightning are the same weather, drawn in the painting's own renderer rather than in CSS.

rules.name: The Lit Slip Rule
rules.body: Only marble slips cast shadows, and always soft and umber (black in shade). No other surface is lifted.

dos: **Do** take every colour from the tone context: write `tone-*` utilities and wrap shaded rooms in `.on-shade`.
**Do** bring new content in with light: tie it to `--room-light` (the `.lit` / `.lit-dim` mixes) or the haze uniform, and keep it fully visible by default.
**Do** label every exhibit with real data in a cartela: SMK inventory for casts, real tags for projects, artist, title, date and collection for paintings.

**Do** mark each painting stage with `data-guide-cover`, give it an `sr-only` heading or list carrying the same words its captions show one at a time, and use `aria-live="polite"` for counters that change with scroll.

**Do** give every reduced-motion path a still layout: stages stop pinning; the method, oracle and giants rooms become the whole painting (70svh, on the portico shade) above a hairline-ruled list; layers, storm and lightning stop with the clock; pointer light and parallax stop; the treasury's coins lie still under a fixed lamp.

**Do** ship every raster with its provenance written by `impeccable embed-prompt`, recording origin, licence, processing and use: a `<file>.json` sidecar beside each WebP (paintings, depth maps, statues, colonnade plates, and the SAM cut-out layers and LaMa-filled plates of animated paintings), an `impeccable:prompt` metadata entry inside PNG and JPEG files (project screenshots, the Open Graph card).
**Do** keep the sky colour identical in CSS, the painting renderer and the gallery scene, so haze lands exactly on the page.
donts: **Don't** use gradients other than light and haze: the name's glint, scrims taken from a painting's own umber, the portico's shaded roof and floor over its view and the shade behind its sign, the feathers that ease that view into the sky, and the curtain's mask are the whole list.
**Don't** round corners on buttons, cartelas, cards or panels.
**Don't** set the name's Cormorant SC anywhere but the name, or let reading text flare.
**Don't** set small gold type on the sky in gilding or light gold; use deep gold, or gilding-for-ink over a painting.
**Don't** shadow anything but marble slips, and never with hard or offset shadows.
**Don't** replace a room's local-language title with its Greek name.
